title: Scientists Built a Machine to Twist Oreos #shorts

lines.text: Why does Oreo cream always stick to just one side? Scientists built a machine to find out.
In twenty twenty-two, MIT engineers made the Oreometer, a gadget that twists Oreos using pennies and rubber bands.
They tested regular, double, and mega stuffing, plus different flavors.
The result? The cream almost always stuck to one side.
Twisting an Oreo takes about as much force as turning a doorknob.
Researchers suspect the factory, where the cream lands on the first wafer before the second one arrives.
So, why does the cream stick to one side? Scientists built a machine, and no twist could fix it.

sources: Owens, Fan, Hart, McKinley. On Oreology, the fracture and flow of milk's favorite cookie. Physics of Fluids (Kitchen Flows special issue), April 2022

facts.device: Oreometer: 3D-printable rheometer-style device twisting an Oreo with pennies and rubber bands (MIT MechE)
facts.tested: regular, Double Stuf, Mega Stuf, plus dark chocolate and golden wafers
facts.finding: cream almost always stuck to one wafer regardless of filling or flavor
facts.force: about the torque of turning a doorknob, roughly one-tenth of a bottle cap
facts.cause: suspected: cream dispensed onto first wafer before second is added (researchers' hypothesis)
